findings.title: `Documenter` appears bare (unbacktick­ed) twice in the module docstring, backticked once
locations: ext/GBGCodingToolsDocumenterExt.jl:4 — "The Documenter extension of `GBGCodingTools`: it defines the body of"
ext/GBGCodingToolsDocumenterExt.jl:6 — "so no shim call ever loads Documenter."
findings.description: RULE.DOC.FORMATTED requires every code identifier backticked, never bare. `Documenter` is the name of the extension's trigger package (used as a real identifier at line 10, `using GBGCodingTools, Documenter`), and the docstring itself gets it right in the middle of the same paragraph — line 5, "It loads only where `Documenter` is" — but leaves it bare at the start of the paragraph (line 4, "The Documenter extension") and at the end (line 6, "loads Documenter."). The inconsistency within one three-line docstring makes it an easy, low-risk fix rather than a stylistic judgment call.
findings.resolution_hint: Backtick both bare occurrences: "The `Documenter` extension of `GBGCodingTools`" and "so no shim call ever loads `Documenter`."

findings.title: `check`'s `verb` argument is never bound as its own code span (ARGCOV run from the signature)
locations: ext/GBGCodingToolsDocumenterExt.jl:14-19 — `check(verb::AbstractString, code::Integer)` / "Turns a verb's exit code into a build failure: returns `nothing` when `code == 0`, else throws `ErrorException(\"gbg <verb> returned <code>\")`."
findings.description: RULE.DOC.ARGCOV requires every signature argument, enumerated from the signature, to be documented in the body as a plain span or a span carrying its default. `code` is bound this way (the literal `code == 0` span). `verb` is not: it is referenced only as the common noun "a verb" in prose and inside the `<verb>` placeholder of the error-message template, never as a `` `verb` `` span naming the actual parameter — a mechanical sweep run from the signature would not find `verb` bound.
findings.resolution_hint: Add a `` `verb` `` span, e.g. "turns `verb`'s exit code into a build failure", so the sweep finds both parameters bound by name.
